metadata.title: Cade Otton a Low-End TE2 for Week 8
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton has made a minimal impact on the field lately. Otton has held without a catch during last week's win over the Carolina Panthers. Over the last three games, Otton has been held to four receptions for 29 receiving yards and zero touchdowns. It has been an ugly stretch of play for Otton, but he does draw a favorable matchup against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8. A defense that has struggled to contain tight ends this season. They've allowed over 60 receiving yards per game to tight ends and currently rank 29th against the pass in general. It's a juicy matchup for Otton, but fantasy managers have little reason to believe he's going to get more involved. He ranks as Rotoballer's TE29 and is a low-end TE2 for this upcoming NFC South matchup.

metadata.title: Cade Otton silent in Sunday win
metadata.description: Cade Otton failed to haul in his only target in the Buccaneers' 43-13 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Otton was running wind sprints once again, and now has just three targets and four receiving yards to his name over the last two weekends of football. He's best left on waivers right now, as his value has primarily been when the Bucs are without any notable receivers.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - No catches in blowout win
metadata.description: Otton failed to catch his only target during Sunday's 43-13 win over the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: Otton went without a reception for the first time this season, and he has now combined to reel in one of three targets for four yards over the last two weeks. Tampa Bay leaned on the run in the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield, and Mayfield completed seven of 11 passes for just 64 yards in the victory. Otton figures to have much better days ahead as his quarterback gets back up to speed, and the tight end's first shot at getting back on track will come Week 8 against Atlanta.

metadata.title: Cade Otton is Barely on Fantasy Radar for Week 7
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton has barely been a factor lately. Over the last two games, Otton has hauled in four receptions for 29 yards. The hope is that the return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Week 7 will boost the overall value of Otton. Also, the absence of top wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) could play a factor as well. The hope is that Otton bounces back against the Carolina Panthers this weekend, but fantasy managers still shouldn't trust him as a starting option. He'll offer a low floor even with Egbuka out and Mayfield back under center. Fantasy managers should keep Otton on the bench until he proves he can offer viable value.

metadata.title: Cade Otton quiet Sunday
metadata.description: Cade Otton caught 1-of-2 targets for four yards in the Buccaneers 26-19 loss against the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Otton remains off the fantasy radar with Jalon Daniels behind center.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - One catch in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Otton caught one of two targets for four yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Otton was targeted on just two of Jalon Daniels' 43 pass attempts, good for a lousy 4.7 percent share. The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and has been held below 40 yards in five of six contests. He's a low-floor fantasy option at the position who is best left on waivers.

metadata.title: Cade Otton Stays on TE2 Radar for Week 6
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton was once again fairly quiet during last week's win over the Dallas Cowboys. He hauled in three of his four targets for 25 yards in the victory. Otton hasn't given fantasy managers much to cheer about this season. The 27-year-old has been held to under 40 receiving yards in every game besides one. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect much to change with backup quarterback Jalon Daniels remaining under center for the Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Otton doesn't have a very high ceiling and cannot be trusted as anything more than a TE2 right now.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Logs three catches in victory Thursday night
metadata.description: Otton caught three of four targets for 25 yards in a 24-16 win over Dallas on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Otton was active early, catching two passes on the Buccaneers' first drive. However, he logged only two more targets and one more reception -- an 11-yarder that helped set up a field goal in the third quarter -- the rest of the way. The 25 total yards were a low mark so far this season for the veteran tight end, who has caught between three and five passes in all five of Tampa Bay's games so far. That at least gives him a reliable floor, but Otton doesn't have a very high week-to-week fantasy ceiling.

metadata.title: Cade Otton catches three passes in win
metadata.description: Cade Otton caught three of four targets for 25 yards in the Bucs' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Otton had two of his three catches on the first drive, and wasn't heard from much afterwards. The passing offense under Jaylon Daniels is still effective, just not explosive. Things get done, but maybe not in a fantasy-friendly manner. That's going to hurt Otton's fantasy value until something changes.

metadata.title: Cade Otton Sticks in TE2 Range for Week 5
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton has been quiet through the first four weeks of the season. Heading into Week 5, Otton has recorded 15 receptions with 157 receiving yards and zero touchdowns. He has an increased chance of finding the end zone this Thursday against the struggling Dallas Cowboys defense. A unit that has allowed three touchdowns to tight ends through the first four games of the season. Otton hauled in four of his six targets for 37 yards during last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Fantasy managers should expect Otton to remain in the TE2 range for this upcoming Thursday Night matchup.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Leads team in receiving Week 4
metadata.description: Otton caught four of six targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 17-14 loss to the Packers.
metadata.analysis: With rookie Jalon Daniels making his first career start, he leaned on Otton in the passing game, and the tight end ended up leading the team in receiving yards despite seeing one fewer target than Chris Godwin. Otton has turned 23 targets into 15 catches for 157 yards through four games this season.

metadata.title: Cade Otton leads Bucs in receiving in Week 4
metadata.description: Cade Otton caught four of his six targets for 37 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Otton was busy in quarterback Jalon Daniels' NFL debut, serving as a safety valve for the rookie. The veteran tight end has drawn exactly six targets in three straight games for Tampa. Overall, he has 15 catches for 157 yards through four games. He will be a low-end TE2 in Week 5 vs. the Cowboys.

metadata.title: Cade Otton Remains on TE2 Radar for Week 4
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton is coming off his best performance of the season. Last week, Otton hauled in three of his six targets for 56 yards in the loss to the Minnesota Vikings. His value seemed to be on the rise, but it'll now take a hit with quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb) heading to the sideline for at least the next three weeks. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be making his first career start against the Green Bay Packers in Week 4. Most of the offensive skilled players will take a hit with Daniels under center. Fantasy managers should keep Otton on the TE2 radar for this upcoming matchup.

metadata.title: Cade Otton's Stock Takes a Hit with Quarterback Downgrade
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton is trending in the wrong direction for fantasy football. Otton has maintained a steady role early in the season, logging at least an 89% snap share and five targets in all three games so far. However, a quarterback downgrade will have major ramifications for his outlook going forward. Otton, whose sizable role has resulted in an underwhelming TE22 rank so far, will now begin catching passes from Jalon Daniels, who will earn the start in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined. The snap share and target volume could be sustainable, but his reception and yardage totals will likely be scaled back with the undrafted free agent at quarterback. Otton is projected to fall outside the top 24 fantasy tight ends by the time this week's game is all said and done. Redraft managers should consider replacing him with a higher-upside option.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Produces 56 yards in Week 3 defeat
metadata.description: Otton tallied three catches on six targets for 56 yards Sunday in a loss to the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Otton finished second on the Bucs in both targets and receiving yards in his best game of 2026 to date. The majority of the tight end's receiving yardage came on a 37-yard connection with Baker Mayfield midway through the second quarter. However, Mayfield is expected to miss at least three weeks of action due to a thumb injury, so Otton will be working with rookie undrafted QB Jalon Daniels over the next few games.

metadata.title: Cade Otton a safety blanket for the Buccaneers Sunday
metadata.description: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Otton was second on the team in targets on the day. He has seen at least five targets in all three weeks to start the season. He'll remain a high floor tight end play next week against the Packers.

metadata.title: Cade Otton Stays on TE2 Radar
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton is coming off a decent performance against the Cleveland Browns last week. The 27-year-old hauled in five of his six targets for 38 yards in the loss. He led the team with his five catches, but he was third on the team in receiving yards. The expectation is that his role as a pass-catcher will be reduced this week. The Minnesota Vikings come to town this weekend for a tough Week 3 matchup. Otton is likely to be used more as a pass-blocker against the blitz-happy Vikings defensive line. He should offer low-end TE2 value, but most fantasy managers can find a more reliable option for this weekend.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Leads Bucs with five catches in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Otton caught five of six targets for 38 yards during the Buccaneers' 23-19 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Four of the five passes Otton caught went for 10 yards or less, but he still led all Bucs pass catchers with five receptions while finishing third in receiving yards to Tez Johnson (49) and Chris Godwin (46). Otton played 58 of 65 offensive snaps (89.2 percent) and has served as security blanket in the passing game for Baker Mayfield. That said, Otton may be used more as a pass blocker Week 3 against the Vikings and their blitz-happy defense under defensive coordinator Brian Flores.

metadata.title: Cade Otton catches five passes Sunday
metadata.description: Cade Otton caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
metadata.analysis: Otton was a safety blanket all afternoon for Baker Mayfield. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Cade Otton Remains TE2 for Week 2
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton played 98 percent of the offensive snaps during last week's season opener against the Cincinnati Bengals. He was on the field for almost all the offensive plays, but still managed to give a lackluster performance. Otton hauled in three of his five targets for 26 yards in the loss. The 27-year-old was third on the team in targets, so there's some hope for him. The Bucs were sloppy with three fumbles in Week 1. They'll look to clean it up in a favorable matchup against the Cleveland Browns in Week 2. There's a chance that Otton gets more involved this weekend, but until he proves otherwise, fantasy managers should consider him a low-upside TE2.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Posts 26 yards in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Otton caught three of five targets for 26 yards in Tampa Bay's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Otton played 56 of 57 offensive snaps and ran 31 routes on Baker Mayfield's 36 dropbacks. His five targets were good for third on the team, trailing only Bucky Irving's seven and Emeka Egbuka's six. Otton plays virtually every snap, but he's a low-floor, low-upside fantasy option who caught just one touchdown last season.

metadata.title: Cade Otton quiet Sunday
metadata.description: Cade Otton caught 3-for-5 targets for 26 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Otton was third on the team in targets, but he was unable to turn it into much production. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Cade Otton Has High-End TE2 Potential for Week 1
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton might be a sneaky option for fantasy managers this weekend. Otton heads into a favorable road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, who were one of the worst defenses this past season. Otton might be asked to do more offensively than fantasy managers might think. The Bucs lost top wide receiver Mike Evans in free agency, and fellow wideout Jalen McMillan (knee) is doubtful for the season opener. Otton is entering his fifth season in Tampa Bay and has built good chemistry with quarterback Baker Mayfield. The 27-year-old has seen 80 or more targets over each of the last two seasons. Given the injuries and the matchup, Otton should offer high-end TE2 value for Week 1.

metadata.title: Cade Otton an Intriguing Tight End Streamer in Week 1
metadata.description: Across 16 games in 2025, Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton recorded 59 catches for 572 yards and one touchdown on 81 targets. While the 27-year-old does not profile as a consistent fantasy producer, he enters 2026 as the clear top receiving tight end in Tampa and may have an opportunity to see increased usage in the early portion of the season. Buccaneers wideouts Emeka Egbuka (toe) and Jalen McMillan (knee) are dealing with lingering injuries that limited their availability throughout the summer. While both players logged full practices on Wednesday, Tampa Bay could look to manage their workloads early on. Otton also has a favorable matchup on paper in Week 1 against the Cincinnati Bengals, who fielded one of the NFL's worst defenses in 2025. As a deep-league streamer, Otton could have some appeal on the waiver wire for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Remains No. 1 TE on depth chart
metadata.description: Otton is listed as the No. 1 TE on the Buccaneers' unofficial depth chart.
metadata.analysis: Aside from adding sixth-round rookie Bauer Sharp to the TE room this offseason, it's status quo for the position group in 2026, with all of Otton, Payne Durham and Ko Kieft back. Otton himself re-signed with Tampa Bay on a three-year, $30 million contract in March to retain his standing as the team's top tight end. Over the last two regular seasons, he's recorded exactly 59 catches on both occasions, totaling 1,172 yards and five touchdowns on 168 targets across 30 contests.

metadata.title: Cade Otton a Potential Early-Season Streamer
metadata.description: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton has rarely flashed for fantasy since coming into the league as a fourth-round pick in 2022, but he has reliably done what's been asked of him, and with the Buccaneers opening the season with a receiver room at less than full strength, he could again be asked to step up. Emeka Egbuka (toe) and Jalen McMillan (knee) have both been dealing with lingering injuries, putting their Week 1 availability in question. Even if both should suit up for the Buccaneers' season-opener against the Bengals, they could each face a snap count of sorts, providing Otton with a pathway to heavier involvement and an increased target share. Cracking the top 15 of the position four times in 2025, Otton has become a prototypical streamer, and although he ranks as RotoBaller's TE24 for 2026, he has the opportunity to re-enter that conversation straight out of the gate, making him a potentially usable piece early in the year.

metadata.title: Cade Otton - Back at practice
metadata.description: Otton (undisclosed) returned to practice Tuesday, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
metadata.analysis: Otton missed about a week of action for the Bucs, and it's unclear if he'll play in Friday's preseason finale against Jacksonville. Last season, Otton matched his career high with 59 catches across 16 regular-season games, turning them into 572 yards and one touchdown. He's expected to be the third or fourth option in Tampa Bay's passing attack in 2026.
